newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka's '96 GDP growth lower at 3.8 pct-ADB.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka's '96 GDP growth lower at 3.8 pct-ADB.

text.p: Sri Lanka's gross domestic product (GDP) growth in 1996 slowed to 3.8 percent, sharply lower than 5.6 percent growth in the previous year, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) said in its annual report on Thursday.

"The slowdown was primarily due to problems in the agricultural sector, which shrank by 0.9 percent, and due to power shortages, which hit the manufacturing sector," the Manila-based bank's report said.
It said paddy output fell by 23 percent due to the failure of the northeast monsoon, forcing Sri Lanka to import 350,000 tonnes of rice in 1996.

"The industry sector, accounting for about one third of the GDP, grew by only 6.2 percent because of the slow growth of the manufacturing subsector, which suffered from prolonged power cuts in the second quarter of the year."
The report did not give comparative figures for industry sector growth.
The bank forecast GDP growth of 5.7 percent for 1997 and 5.9 percent for 1998.
